This maize plot is big for us, almost two and a half hectares, and I am intercropping as we always do here in Lindi — it spreads the risk if rains are poor. Chemical fertilizer is expensive and hard to find in our area, so I will not buy any; instead I will spread what little manure we have from the goats near the house. I will plant seed I saved from last season because improved seed is costly and not always available at our local market. I will rely mostly on my own hands and my children for weeding, but I will hire a few people to help clear the land at the start because two hectares is too much for one family to prepare in time for the rains.
